title: Start here: Gopher is the interface; Semantic Source Control is the historical truth
summary: Use Gopher as the bounded navigation/edit/tooling membrane and Semantic Source Control (SSC) as the authority for stable source identity, accepted history, source levels, semantic deltas, impact and tracked external-operation identity. A Gopher page/result is a projection of SSC evidence, never a replacement repository and never bearer authority.
invariants: Paths, ZIP members and Gopher selectors are carriers/navigation; SSC entity identity is stable across path movement.
A Gopher result page may render SSC state but cannot redefine or mint SSC history.
An edit creates an unaccepted candidate revision; it does not create a new accepted source level.
Gopher access policy and SSC acceptance authority are separate gates and both must hold for a mutating acceptance operation.
